title: Pressure ulcers: site, stage and healing
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's pressure ulcer, if any.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for pressure ulcer.

HPI
The patient is a 77-year-old female presenting today for a scheduled evaluation of a pressure ulcer located over the sacrum. She reports that the wound has been persistent and is causing localized discomfort. She has been managed with regular repositioning and topical treatments. She notes that while the area remains painful, she has not experienced any drainage or fever since the last visit. She expresses a desire to continue her current treatment regimen to promote wound healing.

Medication List
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
- Amlodipine 5 mg daily

Review of Systems
The patient reports no recent fevers, chills, or night sweats. She denies any shortness of breath or chest pain. She reports no new-onset joint pain or vision changes. She denies any significant changes in appetite or bowel habits.

Social History
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is a retired teacher and enjoys gardening and reading. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, Stroke.
Father: Coronary Artery Disease.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.4 F
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Albumin: 3.8 g/dL
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: The patient appears well-nourished and is in no acute distress.
Skin: Physical examination reveals a stage 3 pressure ulcer over the sacrum. The wound measures approximately 3 cm x 4 cm. The wound bed shows visible granulation tissue and some slough. The surrounding skin is intact but erythematous.

Assessment
1. Stage 3 pressure ulcer of the sacrum.

Plan
The patient will continue with a regimen of wound cleansing and topical dressing changes. I have instructed the patient and her caregivers to maintain a strict turning schedule every two hours to reduce pressure on the sacrum. We will monitor the wound for any changes in size or appearance. The patient will return in two weeks for a follow-up wound assessment.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Pressure ulcer of the sacral region, stage 3: L89.153 (HCC 381).

distractors.why: The stage is documented: it decides the code and the HCC.
